substances.name: MDMA
substances.notes: Timings vary with dose, purity and food. A redose, if any, is usually one smaller dose; more mostly adds side effects and a worse next day.

oral.text: Usually starts 20 to 70 minutes after swallowing. Early on you may feel restless, tingly, jaw-tight or a bit sick before the warm, open feeling arrives. Not feeling it yet is normal; taking more now can mean both doses hit together.

insufflated.text: Snorting MDMA does not make it start much sooner. Wait out the full onset window before deciding the first dose isn't working, or both doses may land together.

rectal.text: Effects can take over an hour to start. Wait out the full onset window before deciding the first dose isn't working, or both doses may land together.

stacking.text: A second dose pushes the amount in your blood higher than the first did, yet usually feels weaker. It adds strain on your heart and blood pressure without bringing the first rush back.

effects.summary: Warm, open and chatty, with energy and music and touch feeling stronger. Also jaw clenching, sweating, a fast heartbeat and wide pupils.

afterEffects.text: Tiredness, low mood, irritability and poor sleep are common for a day or two. Some people feel flat or tearful for up to a week. Rest, eat well and go easy on yourself.

harmReduction.text: Test it first. Pills and powder vary a lot in strength and can contain other drugs. Use a reagent kit, or a drug-checking service if the festival has one.
Start low, with half a pill or less until you know how strong it is. A common dose of pure MDMA is around 80 to 125 mg.
If you redose, take one smaller dose, a third to a half of the first, no sooner than 90 minutes in. More than that mostly adds side effects and a worse comedown.
Sip about 200 to 500 ml of water an hour, up to about 700 ml if you're dancing hard. Drinking much more than that can be as dangerous as too little. Electrolyte drinks or salty snacks help.
Take breaks from dancing somewhere cool. Overheating is one of the main dangers, and heat, crowds, hard dancing and other stimulants all make it worse.
Leave at least a few weeks between uses, ideally a few months. Using often makes it work less and makes the low days afterwards worse.

getHelpIf.text: Overheating, confusion, fainting or a seizure: get the medics now and help cool them down.
A bad headache, vomiting or confusion after drinking a lot of water.
Stiff or twitching muscles with a high temperature and agitation, especially with antidepressants.
Chest pain, or a racing or uneven heartbeat that won't settle.

substances.name: Ketamine
substances.notes: Effects build fast and can tip into a k-hole, where moving and talking become hard. Sit or lie down somewhere safe, and avoid it with alcohol or GHB.

insufflated.text: A bump usually hits within a few minutes and peaks within about an hour. Another bump on top can tip you into a k-hole where you can't move or talk safely. Sit down first, and never mix it with alcohol or GHB.

oral.text: Swallowed ketamine is slower and less predictable, taking up to an hour or more to start. Not feeling it yet is normal; taking more now can stack into a k-hole. Sit down somewhere safe.

stacking.text: Each bump lands on top of the last, and the short high makes it easy to keep going. Stacking bumps is how people end up in a k-hole, unable to move or talk safely.

effects.summary: Floaty and detached, with a numb body, wobbly walking and blurred vision. More can cut you off from your surroundings (a k-hole).

afterEffects.text: Grogginess and poor coordination can last a few hours after it wears off. Frequent use can damage the bladder: pain, needing to pee often, or blood in your pee.

harmReduction.text: Sit or lie down before it kicks in, somewhere safe, away from crowds, stairs and water. Falls and choking are the main dangers.
Start with a small bump and let it fully come up before deciding on more. Around 100 mg snorted is often enough for a k-hole.
Don't mix with alcohol, GHB or benzos. Together they can cause blackouts, vomiting and passing out.
Don't take big doses alone or in a crowd. Have a friend with you who knows what you've taken.
Use your own straw, and rinse your nose with salt water once the peak has passed.
If peeing hurts, or you need to go much more often, stop using it and see a doctor.

getHelpIf.text: Can't be woken, or vomits while out of it: put them on their side and get the medics.
Slow or noisy breathing, especially after mixing with alcohol or GHB.
A bad fall or a knock to the head.

substances.name: Cocaine
substances.notes: Very short effects and a sharp dip afterwards drive frequent redosing. Each dose adds strain on the heart, more so with alcohol, other stimulants, heat or dancing hard.

insufflated.text: A line kicks in within minutes, peaks fast and fades within an hour or so. The urge to do another as it fades is the drug, not a sign you need more. Each line adds strain on your heart, so space them out and drink water.

stacking.text: The high fades within minutes and the pull for another line is strong. Each line still adds to the load on your heart, even when it feels like less.

effects.summary: A short burst of confidence, energy and talking, then a dip that pulls you to take more. Raises heart rate and blood pressure.

afterEffects.text: The comedown comes quickly: low mood, tiredness and cravings, worse after big or frequent doses. Staying up for days raises the risk of paranoia.

harmReduction.text: Its short high drives line after line. Decide your limit before you start and keep the rest out of reach.
Street cocaine is often cut with other drugs, such as levamisole. Test it if you can.
Use your own straw. Shared straws can pass on hepatitis C. Saline spray before and after helps protect your nose.
Hard dancing in the heat, or mixing with other stimulants, adds to overheating and strain on your heart.
Even modest doses can cause sudden heart problems in some people, so start small.

getHelpIf.text: Chest pain, or a racing or uneven heartbeat: get the medics now.
A sudden severe headache, weakness on one side, or slurred speech.
Overheating, a seizure, or seeing or hearing things that aren't there.

substances.name: Amphetamine
substances.notes: Long-lasting. Doses taken late keep you awake well past the end of the night.

oral.text: Swallowed speed can take up to 45 minutes to start and keeps building for an hour or two after that. Not feeling the full effect yet is normal; more now means a longer, harder night and no sleep.

insufflated.text: A line starts within minutes but keeps building for up to an hour and a half. Wait for it to level off before deciding you need more; it lasts for hours.

effects.summary: Long-lasting energy, focus and talking, less hunger, a fast heartbeat, jaw clenching and trouble sleeping.

afterEffects.text: Expect a long comedown: tiredness, low mood and poor sleep for the rest of the night and often the next day. Your heart rate can stay raised for hours.

harmReduction.text: Street speed varies a lot in purity, and these doses are for the pure drug. Start small and wait: up to 45 minutes when swallowed.
It lasts many hours, so a late dose means no sleep. Plan your last one early in the night.
It hides hunger and thirst. Keep sipping water and eat something during the night.
Take breaks from dancing and stay cool. Overheating is a real risk.
Avoid mixing with other stimulants or with downers; both add strain on your heart.

getHelpIf.text: Chest pain, or a racing or uneven heartbeat: get the medics now.
Overheating, confusion or a seizure.
Paranoia, or seeing or hearing things, that won't settle.

substances.name: Mephedrone
substances.notes: Strong urge to redose as it wears off. Plan a limit before you start.

oral.text: Bombed or swallowed, it can take up to 45 minutes to start, then builds for another half hour. Not feeling it yet is normal. The craving for more is strong with this one; stick to the limit you planned.

insufflated.text: A line starts within minutes and builds over the next half hour. The craving for more is strong as it fades; that is the drug, not a sign you need more. Stick to the limit you planned.

stacking.text: The effects are short and the urge to redose is very strong. Decide your limit before you start and let the wait timer hold you to it.

effects.summary: Euphoria, chattiness and energy, with a strong urge to take more. Sweating, a fast heartbeat and cold fingers are common.
sideEffects: Cold or blue fingers and toes

afterEffects.text: The comedown can last for hours and sometimes into the next day, with low mood, anxiety, poor sleep and cravings that make it hard to stop.

harmReduction.text: The urge to redose is strong. Weigh out what you'll allow yourself for the night in advance and leave the rest at home.
Start low. Snorted, it starts within minutes, and strength varies between batches.
Don't mix with antidepressants or with other serotonin drugs such as MDMA.
Stay cool and take breaks. Cold or blue fingers mean it's narrowing your blood vessels.

getHelpIf.text: Chest pain, or a racing or uneven heartbeat: get the medics now.
Overheating, confusion or a seizure.
Fingers or toes turning blue and staying cold or numb.

substances.name: LSD
substances.notes: Lasts most of a day. Strength per tab varies a lot, so start low with a new batch. PsychonautWiki lists LSD as sublingual; its figures are used here for tabs held in the mouth then swallowed.

oral.text: Can take up to an hour and a half to notice, and keeps building for another hour or more. Wait at least 3 hours before taking more, or both doses can arrive at once. It lasts 8 to 14 hours either way.

stacking.text: Tolerance starts within hours, so a second dose mid-trip adds less than you expect and mostly makes the trip last longer.

effects.summary: Changes to sight, sound, time and thinking, with strong emotions. A long trip that builds slowly and makes sleep hard.

afterEffects.text: Sleep is often hard for hours after the trip ends, and you may feel drained or thoughtful the next day.

harmReduction.text: It's slow and long. It can take over an hour to start, so don't take more because it seems weak: a second dose makes the trip longer and stronger.
Tabs vary in strength, and some sold as LSD are other drugs. Test with a reagent kit if you can.
Have a sober friend nearby, especially the first time or at a higher dose, and know where the welfare tent is.
Cannabis and stimulants can make the trip much more intense or anxious. Go easy if you mix.
Avoid it if you or close family have had psychosis, and never mix it with lithium or tramadol.

getHelpIf.text: Panic that won't settle: find a calm friend or the welfare tent. It will pass.
Get medical help for a seizure, or if someone may hurt themselves or others.

substances.name: Mushrooms
substances.notes: Strength varies by species and batch. Effects take a while to build; eating more early makes the peak much stronger.

oral.text: Usually starts 20 to 60 minutes after eating, then builds for another hour or so. Yawning, an uneasy stomach or feeling odd is common early on. Not feeling much yet is normal; eating more now can make the peak far stronger.

stacking.text: Tolerance builds almost straight away, so more mushrooms mid-trip add less than you expect and mostly make the trip last longer.

effects.summary: Visual changes, strong emotions, laughter or deep thoughts, and often nausea early on. Mood and setting shape the trip.

afterEffects.text: Tiredness and an emotional or thoughtful mood can last into the next day.

harmReduction.text: Strength varies a lot between mushrooms and batches. Start small and wait at least 2 hours before deciding to take more.
Be sure what they are. Wild mushrooms are easily mistaken for poisonous ones.
Have a sober friend nearby, especially the first time or at a higher dose, and know where the welfare tent is.
Cannabis and stimulants can make the trip much more intense or anxious. Go easy if you mix.
Avoid them if you or close family have had psychosis, and never mix them with lithium or tramadol.

getHelpIf.text: Panic that won't settle: find a calm friend or the welfare tent. It will pass.
Get medical help for a seizure, or if someone may hurt themselves or others.

substances.name: 2C-B
substances.notes: Small changes in dose make a big difference. Snorting or plugging is faster, stronger and shorter than swallowing.

oral.text: Can take anywhere from 20 minutes to 2 hours to start, then builds for another hour or so. A body rush, chills or a queasy stomach are common early on. Not feeling it yet is normal; small extra amounts make a big difference.

insufflated.text: Snorting it hits within minutes and is much more intense. It keeps building for up to half an hour, so wait before deciding you need more.

rectal.text: Starts within about 20 minutes and is stronger than swallowing the same amount. Wait for it to build before deciding you need more.

effects.summary: Visuals and body buzz with energy and euphoria; more brings stronger visuals. Nausea while coming up is common.

afterEffects.text: Usually mild: a few hours of tiredness or trouble sleeping after it wears off.

harmReduction.text: Very dose-sensitive: a few milligrams make a big difference, and a snorted dose is about half a swallowed one.
Powder or pills sold as 2C-B can be something else. Test it if you can.
Avoid hard exertion, and keep an eye on your heart rate and temperature, especially if you have a heart condition.
Have a sober friend around, and avoid mixing with stimulants, cannabis, lithium or tramadol.

getHelpIf.text: Overheating, confusion or a seizure: get the medics now.
Panic that won't settle: find a calm friend or the welfare tent. It will pass.

substances.name: GHB
substances.notes: The gap between a dose that feels good and one that knocks you out is small. Measure exactly, wait at least 2 hours between doses, and never mix with alcohol or ketamine. GBL acts faster and is stronger per millilitre.

oral.text: Can take up to an hour to kick in. Many overdoses happen when people take more too soon, so wait at least 2 hours. Never mix with alcohol. If someone can't be woken, put them on their side and get medical help.

effects.summary: Relaxed, euphoric and sociable, like alcohol. The gap between a good dose and passing out is very small.

afterEffects.text: Some people feel groggy for a few hours. Regular use builds dependence, and stopping suddenly after daily use can bring withdrawal that needs a doctor.

harmReduction.text: Measure every dose with an oral syringe, and shake the bottle first: strong liquid can settle at the bottom.
Wait at least 2 hours before taking more. Many overdoses come from redosing too soon.
Never mix with alcohol, even a little, or with other downers. It can knock you out, even hours apart.
Grams and millilitres aren't the same, and GBL is much stronger than GHB. Check which one you have.
Dilute each dose in water or juice and drink it straight away.
Don't use it alone. If you feel dizzy or sick, tell someone and lie on your side.

getHelpIf.text: Can't be woken: put them on their side and call the medics. Don't leave them to sleep it off.
A seizure, slow breathing, or vomiting while drowsy.

substances.name: Cannabis
substances.notes: Edibles are slow and long. Smoking is quick and short. Strength varies a lot by product.

oral.text: Edibles can take up to 2 hours to start and another hour to build. This is the classic one to take too much of: not feeling it yet is normal. Eating more now can mean a very long, rough night.

smoked.text: Felt within minutes and peaks within the first half hour or so. Wait for it to settle before having more, especially if you've also been drinking.

effects.summary: Relaxed, giggly or hungry, with changes to time and senses. Edibles start late and hit harder. Anxiety or paranoia can happen.

afterEffects.text: Grogginess can last into the next morning, and longer after edibles.

harmReduction.text: Edibles can take up to 2 hours to kick in. Have a small piece and wait before having more.
Strength varies a lot between products. Start small, especially if you don't use it often.
It can make psychedelics and stimulants much more intense or anxious. Go easy if you mix.
If it gets too much, find a quiet spot, sit down and sip water. It passes with time.
Avoid it if you or close family have had psychosis.

getHelpIf.text: Fainting or chest pain: get the medics.
Panic that won't settle: find a calm friend or the welfare tent.

substances.name: Alcohol
substances.notes: Timings are per drink. Alcohol makes most other depressants far more dangerous, especially GHB and ketamine.

oral.text: A drink keeps hitting harder for up to about 50 minutes after you have it, so you'll feel drunker than you do now. Space drinks out and have water in between.

effects.summary: Relaxed and less inhibited at first, then slower reactions, poor balance and judgement. Dehydrating, and risky with downers.

afterEffects.text: A hangover the next day: headache, tiredness, nausea and low mood, sometimes into the day after.

harmReduction.text: Pace yourself and have water between drinks. Spreading drinks over hours keeps you in control.
Never mix with GHB, benzos or opioids, and go easy with ketamine. Together they can stop your breathing.
If you take regular medicines, check with a doctor or pharmacist before drinking.

getHelpIf.text: Can't be woken, or breathing is slow: put them on their side and call the medics.
Vomiting while very drowsy or confused.

substances.name: Nitrous oxide
substances.notes: Lasts a minute or two. Breathe normal air between balloons and sit down; never inhale straight from a canister or cracker.

other.text: Hits within seconds and is gone within a few minutes. Sit down before a balloon, and take some normal breaths between them so you don't pass out.

effects.summary: A brief rush of giggly, floaty, dizzy feelings that fades within minutes. Falling over is common, so sit down.

afterEffects.text: Usually gone within half an hour. Heavy or frequent use can cause lasting numbness and nerve damage by using up vitamin B12.

other.unitNote: gas; one small cartridge holds 8 g

harmReduction.text: Sit down before you inhale. Falls are the most common injury.
Breathe normal air between balloons. Nitrous on its own starves you of oxygen.
Only use a balloon, never straight from a canister or tank: the gas comes out freezing cold.
If you use it often, take vitamin B12, and stop if your hands or feet tingle or go numb.

getHelpIf.text: Faints and doesn't come round quickly: get the medics.
Numbness, tingling or weakness in hands or feet that lasts: see a doctor.

medications.name: SSRI antidepressants
medications.notes: Usually makes MDMA, LSD and mushrooms feel weaker. Taking more to make up for it is where the risk is. Don't stop your medicine for a festival without talking to your prescriber.

medications.name: MAOI antidepressants
medications.notes: One of the most dangerous medicines to mix with MDMA or stimulants: blood pressure can spike to a crisis. It can also make mushrooms and GHB much stronger. Some drinks react with it too.

medications.name: Benzodiazepines
medications.notes: With GHB or alcohol, the effects stack fast and unpredictably and can knock you out.

medications.name: Opioid painkillers
medications.notes: With GHB, alcohol or ketamine, you can pass out and stop breathing. Stimulants can hide an opioid until they wear off.

medications.name: Tramadol
medications.notes: Makes seizures more likely with MDMA, stimulants and psychedelics, and stacks dangerously with depressants.

medications.name: Lithium
medications.notes: Many reports of seizures with psychedelics, and MDMA brings a high risk of serotonin syndrome. Getting dehydrated (heat, dancing, MDMA, drinking) can push lithium to toxic levels.

medications.name: Pregabalin and gabapentin
medications.notes: With GHB or alcohol it stacks and can slow your breathing. With stimulants and MDMA, seizures are more likely. Gabapentin works the same way, so it gets the same ratings.

medications.name: ADHD stimulants
medications.notes: Rated as amphetamine, which most of these are. Methylphenidate is not rated separately, so it gets the same ratings. Speed on top is more of the same drug.

medications.name: HIV boosters (ritonavir, cobicistat)
medications.notes: Boosters slow how the body clears many party drugs, so a usual dose can be much stronger and last longer. Most other HIV medicines interact less, but check yours with your HIV clinic.

medications.name: SNRI antidepressants
medications.notes: Like SSRIs, they make MDMA feel weaker while its strain on the body stays. Taking more to make up for it adds risk. Don't stop without talking to your prescriber.

medications.name: Tricyclic antidepressants
medications.notes: Can make LSD and other psychedelics much stronger, and the NHS warns stimulants and hallucinogens can be dangerous with them. Also used in low doses for pain and sleep.

medications.name: Bupropion
medications.notes: Raises MDMA levels and makes it last longer. Bupropion makes seizures more likely, and cocaine, stimulants and heavy drinking add to that.

medications.name: Mirtazapine and trazodone
medications.notes: Sedating antidepressants, often taken for sleep. They add to the drowsiness of alcohol, GHB and ketamine, and can make psychedelics feel weaker.

medications.name: Antipsychotics
medications.notes: Can block a lot of what psychedelics and MDMA do, so they may feel weak. Don't take more to make up for it. Adds to the drowsiness of alcohol and GHB.

medications.name: Sleeping pills (Z-drugs)
medications.notes: Work like benzodiazepines. With alcohol or GHB you can stop breathing properly and be very hard to wake.

medications.name: Sodium valproate
medications.notes: Raises GHB levels in the blood, so a usual dose hits harder. Adds to the drowsiness of alcohol.

medications.name: Beta blockers
medications.notes: With cocaine, a beta blocker may let blood pressure rise and the heart's arteries tighten. The evidence is mixed, but cardiologists are cautious.

medications.name: Epilepsy medicines
medications.notes: Stimulants, MDMA, cannabis and drinking can all bring on seizures. Vomiting can wash your medicine out. Never skip a dose at a festival. Valproate is listed separately.

medications.name: Insulin and hypo-causing diabetes tablets
medications.notes: Dancing, not eating and losing track of time can all cause a hypo, and a hypo can look like being drunk or high. Tell a friend you're diabetic and keep sugar on you.

interactions.note: TripSit rates this combination as caution.
TripSit rates this combination as caution.
TripSit rates this combination as caution.
The stimulant adds strain on the heart and can make the 2C-B trip more anxious and harder to handle.
TripSit rates this combination as caution.
Many reports of seizures and psychosis from this combination.
TripSit rates this combination as caution.
